item.title: Giorgia Meloni Enters the History Books, Pursued by Italy’s Far Right
item.author: Donato Paolo Mancini
item.content:encoded: Meloni’s administration on Friday becomes the longest serving government in Italy since the republic was founded after World War II

item.title: Kai-Fu Lee on the Global AI Race
item.content:encoded: Chinese artificial intelligence companies are rapidly closing the gap with their US rivals. But AI pioneer Kai-Fu Lee contends the race between the two is part of a much bigger transformation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Grab of Venezuela Denies China Oil, Billions in Debt Payments
item.author: Bloomberg News
item.content:encoded: Venezuela is becoming a major testing ground for Donald Trump’s hemispheric ambitions, emerging as another potential source of rivalry with China.

item.title: Macron’s Gulf Push Straddles Divide Between Riyadh and Abu Dhabi
item.author: Dinesh Nair, Samy Adghirni and Omar El Chmouri
item.content:encoded: Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman’s recent trip to Paris showed glimpses of the depth of the French-Saudi relationship. He was spotted with Emmanuel Macron at the Esports World Cup, which was moved out of Riyadh due to the Iran war, and the two unveiled deals spanning everything from technology and defense to a €6 billion theme park.

item.title: Serb President Faces Biggest Threat to His Rule After Student-Led Protests
item.author: Misha Savic
item.content:encoded: Aleksandar Vucic has been facing down student-led protests for almost two years. They’ve gone from irritation to a threat to his rule.

item.title: Malaysia Ex-PM Najib Wins Pause on Bankruptcy Proceedings: Edge
item.author: Ram Anand
item.content:encoded: Malaysia’s jailed ex-premier Najib Razak won a court bid to halt bankruptcy proceedings against him over 1.69 billion ringgit ($418 million) in alleged unpaid tax arrears, according to a report by The Edge.

item.title: South Korean Cabinet Revamp Fails to Stem Slide in Lee Support
item.author: Soobin Kim
item.content:encoded: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung’s approval rating slid to a fresh record low, a sign that his surprise cabinet reshuffle failed to immediately shore up public sentiment.

item.title: Japan Needs to Stand Firm Against US Pressure, Lawmaker Says
item.author: Alastair Gale and Sakura Murakami
item.content:encoded: Japan needs to stand firm against US pressure as its close security ally challenges international norms and laws under President Donald Trump’s “America First” agenda, according to a veteran Japanese lawmaker.

item.title: Argentina Is Ramping Up Its Claim to the Falklands. Here’s What to Know.
item.author: Qasim Nauman
item.content:encoded: President Javier Milei has dialed up Argentina’s claim over the British territory, while President Trump has raised questions about longstanding U.S. neutrality on the dispute.

item.title: Greer Says He’s ‘Optimistic’ About Relations With China Before Trump-Xi Summit
item.author: Ryan Chua
item.content:encoded: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer struck a positive tone on relations with China weeks before a summit between President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping, despite underlying disagreements between the two nations.

item.title: Judge Ends Federal Oversight of Teamsters
item.author: Rebecca Davis O’Brien
item.content:encoded: The union and federal prosecutors agreed that organized crime groups had been rooted out of union operations, the judge wrote.

item.title: Argentina’s Milei Revives Bitter Falklands Dispute With UK
item.author: Manuela Tobias and Jonathan Gilbert
item.content:encoded: Argentina’s Javier Milei is reviving his country’s bitter clash with the UK over the Falkland Islands, targeting a new oil project in the disputed area in strident terms as the popularity of his presidency sinks.

item.title: Former Labor Secretary Stoked Dysfunction and Toxicity, Department Report Finds
item.author: Rebecca Davis O’Brien and Lydia DePillis
item.content:encoded: Lori Chavez-DeRemer spent Labor Department funds on personal travel and tolerated harassment in the agency, its inspector general found.

item.title: Trump Taps Army Engineering Official as Acting Secretary
item.author: Chris Cameron
item.content:encoded: The move came days after the resignation of Daniel P. Driscoll, who had clashed with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the purge of top generals in the Army.

item.title: South Korea Paving Way to Send Troops to Hormuz, Reports Say
item.author: Soo-Hyang Choi
item.content:encoded: South Korea has begun preparations for a possible deployment of a naval support ship and troops to the Strait of Hormuz, local media reports said, as President Donald Trump ramped up pressure on the US ally over its lack of support for the war with Iran.

item.title: Trump Attacks Missouri’s High Court Over Redistricting Decision
item.author: John Harney
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump assailed a decision by the Missouri Supreme Court that cast aside a congressional map engineered by state Republicans, likely allowing Democrats to retain a House seat in November’s midterm elections they would’ve almost certainly otherwise lost.

item.title: Trump to Break Ground on Arch Before Getting Approval
item.author: Luke Broadwater and Emily Badger
item.content:encoded: Doug Burgum, the interior secretary, announced plans to start work on the site of the 250-foot-tall triumphal arch. Final approval of the project is still pending.

item.title: JD Vance on Iran: ‘I Wouldn’t Call It a War'
item.content:encoded: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Jim McGovern (D-MA), the top Democrat on the House Rules Committee, says his conversations with constituents are dominated by concerns around the cost of living, arguing voters want Congress focused on lowering prices ahead of the midterm elections. Vladyslav Vlasiuk, Presidential Commissioner for Sanctions Policy of Ukraine, says Congress should pass a sweeping Russia sanctions bill "now," arguing additional economic pressure is needed to constrain Moscow's ability to fund the war. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Powerful Brazil Judge Faces Reckoning Over Ties to $10 Billion Bank Scandal
item.author: Daniel Carvalho and Martha Beck
item.content:encoded: For the past seven years, no member of Brazil’s Supreme Court has exercised its vast powers as forcefully as Alexandre de Moraes.

item.title: Trump Names Adam Telle Acting Army Secretary After Driscoll Exit
item.author: Jen Judson and Derek Wallbank
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump named Adam Telle as acting secretary of the US Army, elevating the current assistant secretary overseeing civil works following the resignation of Army Secretary Dan Driscoll.

item.title: Alger EVP: Still Massive Opportunity for AI
item.content:encoded: Ankur Crawford, Executive Vice President and Portfolio Manager at Alger, says political backlash around AI infrastructure could become a future constraint on data center and chip buildout, though it has not yet materially slowed projects. She argues that much of the opposition is driven by misinformation and that the key risk for investors is confusion, which can create volatility. She speaks with Romaine Bostick & Sally Bakewell on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Administration Asks Supreme Court to Allow Mail Voting Limits
item.author: Abbie VanSickle
item.content:encoded: The justices have been asked to weigh in again on the Trump administration’s efforts to restrict mail voting — this time on whether the plans violate the Constitution.

item.title: Judge Suggests Trump Mail-In Voting Rules Could Cause ‘Major Disenfranchisement’
item.author: Zach Montague
item.content:encoded: Judge Indira Talwani said the Postal Service appeared to be trying a haphazard “experiment” with a new rule that could result in valid ballots being tossed.

item.title: Proposal for White House Visitor Screening Center Advances
item.author: Aishvarya Kavi
item.content:encoded: A federal panel again paved the way for one of President Trump’s construction projects, even as it heard opposition to another proposal to fence in a park north of the White House.

item.title: FCC Tells Judge Trump Clash With ABC Isn’t About Free Speech
item.author: Erik Larson
item.content:encoded: The US Federal Communications Commission asked a judge to toss out ABC’s lawsuit accusing the regulator of waging an unconstitutional “retaliatory campaign” against the network as punishment for programming criticized by the Trump administration.

item.title: JD Vance Says He Wouldn’t Call Iran Conflict a War
item.author: Maggie Haberman
item.content:encoded: In the first White House press briefing since Karoline Leavitt left as press secretary, the vice president suggested that when the conflict would end was up to Tehran.

item.title: Hillary Clinton, Meghan Markle, Lena Dunham and Others Pay Tribute to Gloria Steinem
item.author: Johnny Diaz
item.content:encoded: After Ms. Steinem’s death at 92, celebrities and politicians reflected on her decades of activism for women’s rights and equality.

item.title: Farage’s Bid to Reset Reform UK Fortunes Hit By Undercover Sting
item.author: Alex Wickham
item.content:encoded: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage’s hopes of using a keynote speech at his party’s annual convention to arrest a slide in opinion polls were upended after two of his closest allies were covertly filmed discussing avoiding electoral law to secure foreign donations.

item.title: Supreme Court Asked to Allow Mail Ballot Curbs for Midterms
item.author: Zoe Tillman
item.content:encoded: The Trump administration asked the US Supreme Court to let the Postal Service enforce new rules for mail-in ballots ahead of the November midterm elections, a move that some states have warned would wreak havoc as they prepare to send ballots to voters in the coming days.

item.title: Gloria Steinem, Personification of the Feminist Movement, Dies at 92
item.author: Katharine Q. Seelye
item.content:encoded: She challenged sexist assumptions, helping women develop a sense of self-worth and gain a measure of equality at work, at home and in society at large.

item.title: Rate Rise in Play as Fed Officials Await Inflation Data
item.author: Colby Smith
item.content:encoded: Christopher J. Waller, a Federal Reserve governor, sounded optimistic about inflation’s trajectory but indicated he would support higher rates if progress does not continue.

item.title: Trump’s D.C. Makeover Projects Are ‘Only an Idea,’ Until They’re Much More
item.author: Emily Badger
item.content:encoded: A proposed garden of heroes is following a familiar path in which facts on the ground move faster than the courts and others can keep up.

item.title: Is Letting Only Seniors Vote by Mail Unconstitutional?
item.author: Adam Liptak
item.content:encoded: Federal appeals courts have split on the question, making Supreme Court review likely.

item.title: El-Sayed Wants to Mend Ties With Jewish Democrats, but Some Are Still Not Impressed
item.author: Bayliss Wagner and Steve Friess
item.content:encoded: Lingering concerns about the Senate nominee in Michigan could make it harder for him to assemble a winning coalition.

item.title: Taiwan Gets Rare Win Over China in Spat at South Korean Art Show
item.author: Yian Lee
item.content:encoded: A South Korean art exhibition will allow Taiwanese participants to use the designation “Taiwan Pavilion,” despite Chinese protests, marking a rare win for the island in its fight for international recognition.

item.title: Homeland Security Secretary’s Plane Makes Emergency Landing
item.author: Karoun Demirjian
item.content:encoded: The landing was the latest close call over Washington’s congested airspace to involve a senior government official.

item.title: White House Plans $250,000 Renovation of 2-Lane Bowling Alley
item.author: Mack Liederman
item.content:encoded: A White House spokesman said the alley renovations included fixing broken lights. The project comes as the president has sought a broad overhaul of the White House and its surroundings.

item.title: Judge Blocks Trump’s Second Try to Restrict Birthright Citizenship
item.author: Zach Montague
item.content:encoded: The ruling raised concerns that babies already defined as citizens by the Supreme Court could have their citizenship revoked under an order the president signed in August.

item.title: As Midterms Loom, Democrats Feud Over Defections
item.author: Michael Gold
item.content:encoded: The fight has highlighted party divisions and raised questions about how Democrats will run the House should they win the majority.

item.title: In the Midterms, Will the Nepo-Baby Attack Work?
item.author: Jess Bidgood
item.content:encoded: A New Hampshire senator’s daughter is running for office, and finds her name being used against her.
